chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan ibn Waddah, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
One who recites Surah al-Saff and makes it a habit to recite it in his obligatory and voluntary prayers, Allah will place him in a row with His angels and His messenger prophets, if Allah wills.

key_terms.صَفَّهُ اللَّهُ: Allah will place him in a row

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for regularly reciting Surah al-Saff in prayers?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the transformative power of *idmān* (habitual consistency) in reciting Surah al-Saff, linking the chapter’s theme of divine order to the believer’s eschatological status. It signifies that the reciter is not merely present but is formally 'arranged' (*saffahu*) in the highest ranks alongside angels and prophets, reflecting the Surah’s focus on the unity and discipline of the faithful. This reward underscores the Shia scholarly view that consistent engagement with specific Quranic chapters can elevate one’s spiritual station to the level of the *Anbiyā’ al-Mursalīn* (Messenger Prophets).
